Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: transparent pixel-art building sprite for an existing Grenoble Bomberman game.
Input image 1 is a STYLE AND CAMERA REFERENCE ONLY: preserve its coarse crisp pixel technique, warm red tile roof, blue-gray stone accents and teal shutters. Design a NEW smaller house; do not copy its two-storey geometry.
Primary request: ONE compact ONE-STOREY urban house inspired by Grenoble's Saint-Laurent / quai Perrière historic neighborhood. Butter-yellow ochre lime-plaster facade, pale limestone door and window frames, muted green-blue wooden louvered shutters, a modest dark walnut arched entrance, low-pitched terracotta roof with one small chimney. Simple convincing local French-Alpine urban architecture, no chalet features.
EXACT SHAPE: VERTICAL HEIGHT : HORIZONTAL WIDTH = 1.5 : 1 (width:height 2:3). Designed for a 256px wide x 384px high sprite: roof/chimney is in the TOP 128px; the single-storey facade occupies the LOWER 256px. At corresponding scale, roof eave is exactly one third down the sprite. The facade is a complete rectangular wall right to both side edges and the bottom edge, NOT a house floating in empty margins. Bottom edge horizontal and flush.
Camera: flat straight-on front from slightly above, parallel horizontal eaves, roof surface visible. Same orthographic camera as the reference, no visible side walls, no isometric diamond.
Style: clean deliberately low-resolution pixel art, approximately 64 x 96 source-pixel detail, large clearly defined square pixels, limited harmonious palette, crisp hard stair-step edges, restrained highlights, readable when reduced to 32 x 48. Two shuttered windows flanking the doorway; keep lower middle facade easy to overlay a shop later.
Background: TRUE TRANSPARENT ALPHA outside the house silhouette, especially upper corners beside roof. Building is the only object. No ground, sidewalk, drop shadow, framing border, grid, labels, signage, letters, extra houses, plants, people, landscape or watermark. Full building visible and centered, tightly framed.

NO alpine chalet, no half timber, no mansard roofs.
Crisp low-resolution pixel art with large deliberately square pixels; original game uses 1 tile = 256 output pixels = 64 artwork pixels. Limited palette, flat color clusters, HARD PIXEL EDGES. Avoid all gradients, bloom, soft shading, outlines around individual pixels, smooth rendering or small realistic details.

The COMPLETE facade is a rectangle spanning the full sprite width and down to the bottom edge. Tiny silhouette margin at most; no empty frame. Roof silhouette can have stepped edges and chimneys.
TRUE CLEAR TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND outside the building silhouette. No glow, ambient shadow, cast shadow or colored halo. No ground, base platform, pavement, landscape, people, vegetation, props, labels, grid, measurements, words or watermark. Only the complete building.
EXACT sprite shape VERTICAL HEIGHT : HORIZONTAL WIDTH = 1.5 : 2, so WIDTH:HEIGHT = 4:3 (512px wide x 384px high). ONE STOREY, a broad ochre-cream Grenoble townhouse, warm cream plaster and blue-gray stone corner courses, teal-green shutters, four tall shuttered windows with a dark wood arched entrance near the middle. A single continuous low terracotta roof with two restrained small chimneys. Roof occupies TOP ONE THIRD, rectangular single-storey wall occupies LOWER TWO THIRDS. Wide and low. Readable as 128x96 artwork pixels, displayed at 512x384. This is ONE coherent house, not two disconnected houses.
